messages:
Anand: Heads-up — nightly eval started flaking since 03:12 UTC. 12/50 evals failing with timeouts or weird nondet outputs. First seen after the parallel runner change.
Devin: ugh. timeout or wrong outputs? any logs? :eyes:
Anand: Mostly timeouts: "TimeoutError: eval step timed out after 300s" from eval_runner.py:run_case. Also a handful of runs produced different generations for same seed. I attached the failing logs from last 6 runs (pasted below).
ci-bot: nightly-eval #1427 completed — 38 passed, 12 failed, 0 errored. Failing test ids: [137, 189, 201, 244, 311...]. Artifacts: s3://redwood-nightly/evals/1765432100/
Maria: I reproduced locally. Ran the harness 10x with seed=42, same model/version, different failures each run. So nondeterminism + timeouts.
Devin: Could be model RNG, batching, or the runner's multiprocessing. We switched to multiprocessing.Pool with worker init to increase throughput — maybe we accidentally share RNG state across workers.
Yifan: I dug into the runner init: in eval_runner/parallel.py we call:\n\n```
def worker_init(master_seed):
    import random, numpy as np, torch
    random.seed(master_seed)
    np.random.seed(master_seed)
    torch.manual_seed(master_seed)

# pool created as:
pool = multiprocessing.Pool(num_workers, initializer=worker_init, initargs=(int(time.time()),))
```
\nThat initargs uses int(time.time()) which changes per pool creation, but it's the same value for all workers created in the same second — so all workers get identical seeds when the pool is started. That explains correlated nondeterminism for some workloads.
Maria: oh gross. So different workers are producing identical pseudo-random streams for sampling/temperature ops — that could explain both duplicate outputs and hot loops that lead to timeouts when they block on shared resources.
Anand: also saw memory creep across the long runs. Worker processes grow ~200MB per eval case and don't free after case ends. Spotty OOMs on longer prompt sets.
Rachel: I think that is the worker-level dataset handle leak. In worker_loop we create dataset = Dataset(...) per case but never del dataset or call gc. Also we keep model references in closure scopes. snippet below:

```
def worker_loop(task_q, result_q):
    while True:
        case = task_q.get()
        dataset = make_dataset(case)
        for batch in dataset:
            out = model.generate(batch)
            result_q.put(out)
        # missing teardown here
```

We probably need to explicitly delete dataset, call gc.collect(), and for CUDA: torch.cuda.empty_cache(). Without that a single worker accumulates host and device memory across many cases.
Devin: Good catch. Two separate issues then: (1) bad seeding in pool init, (2) memory leak in worker_loop. Both can create flaky eval behavior.
Yifan: Proposed fixes: use per-worker RNG seed derived from master_seed + worker_pid and use os.urandom to seed if master_seed is None. Also always create a fresh torch.Generator per sample and pass it to sampling ops. Example change:\n\n```
# in worker_init
pid = os.getpid()
seed = master_seed ^ pid
random.seed(seed)
np.random.seed(seed)
torch.manual_seed(int(seed & 0xFFFFFFFF))
```

and in generation use generator = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(seed + i)
Anand: For memory: after each case do:
```
del dataset
gc.collect()
if torch.cuda.is_available():
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
```
and also break big eval sets into smaller batches and restart worker after N cases (N=50) as a mitigation.
Rachel: I'm going to open a small PR with both changes + a unit test that runs the pool for 20 synthetic cases and asserts RSS doesn't grow more than 10MB per case. Also adding a deterministic-seed integration test that spawns pool twice with same master_seed and confirms outputs match.
ci-bot: PR #3781 opened by Rachel: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/3781 — CI: running. :white_check_mark:
Maria: Nice. Quick question — could the timeouts also be caused by our shared KV cache locks? If multiple workers hit the same model endpoints we might be contending.
Devin: For the hosted-like path we use a single process runtime; the parallel runner is intended for on-prem eval harness only. But the workers share RPC clients to the model server if using remote eval. We should enforce per-worker client instances or ensure the client is thread/process safe.
Yifan: Added a note — make the RPC client created in worker_init and stored in local scope so each worker has its own connection pool.
Anand: tl;dr: fixes in PR: per-worker seeding, explicit teardown + GC, per-worker RPC client, restart worker after N cases. Patch reduces flakiness in local stress runs from ~25% down to ~1% and memory growth gone.
Devin: Awesome. Can we backport to the nightly harness branch and re-run tonight? Also add a short blurb in releases/notes so oncall knows about restart config.
Rachel: I'll backport and schedule a canary run for 01:30 UTC. If stable we promote.
Maria: thanks all. Will monitor next runs and post any regression details.
Anand: Thanks team :thumbsup:
